originalTitle: ‘Dangerous power grab’: top Democrats decry USPS system that could thwart mail-in voting – live
summary: A Democratic senator disclosed a whistleblower statement, which warned of potential chaos as the USPS is set to launch a computer system that could derail mail-in voting
content: Hakeem Jeffries condemned the Trump administration in response to the death of Pierre Damas Bel, a Haitian college student who died by suicide after he lost his legal status and was required to wear an ankle monitor. “Like hundreds of thousands of Haitians, Pierre fled dangerous conditions and received temporary protected status to build a better life for himself and patriotically contribute to our nation,” the House Democratic leader said, describing the administration’s actions as “despiable cruelty”. “Instead, Donald Trump’s mass deportation machine ripped away Pierre’s legal status, threatened him with terrifying violence, forced him to wear an ankle monitor and humiliated him in front of his peers.” Bel, a 20-year-old who came to the US in 2024 and lost his temporary protected status in July, died on Monday. NBC News reported that while Bel’s immigration case made its way through the courts ICE required he wear an ankle monitor. Bel said he was “humiliated” by the experience and was bullied. Senator Ed Markey won the Democratic primary in Massachusetts on Tuesday, beating back a challenge from Seth Moulton, a congressman who tried to unseat him by arguing to voters his opponent was too old to be effective at his job. Massachusetts is heavily Democratic, making the senator favored to win a third full term in the November general election, where he faces the Republican nominee John Deaton. The 80-year-old incumbent, according to the Associated Press, easily defeated his 47-year-old rival, at a moment when Democratic voters agonize over the age of some lawmakers, a concern that was amplified by Joe Biden’s disastrous re-election bid in 2024, and Kamala Harris’s subsequent failure to keep Donald Trump from returning to the White House. The Trump administration seized on House Democrats voting against a resolution denouncing socialism, condemning the lawmakers as “sick [and] dangerous”. But there was more in the resolution than language critical of socialism “in all its forms”. The Associated Press reports that it called for the enactment of Trump’s SAVE America Act, a strict voting bill that would ban mail-in ballots and require voters to prove their citizenship. The measure was approved approved 220-192 with a handful of Democrats joining with Republicans in support of the resolution. Democrats described the resolution as a trap ahead of the US midterm elections. “This isn’t a serious bill,” Congressman Josh Gottheimer told Axios. The New Jersey representative is a moderate who has criticized Democratic Socialism. “If you actually want to take on socialism instead of playing political games, you don’t slip in the SAVE [America] Act as a poison pill that you know no Democrat will vote for.” Polls have just closed in Massachusetts where progressive Ed Markey, 80, faces a younger challenger in the US Senate Democratic primary in what is being described as a generational fight. His rival US representative Seth Moulton has argued Markey is too old to serve another term. Read more on the race here: Donald Trump announced on Tuesday that he will nominate Hung Cao to serve as the next secretary of the US Navy. Cao, a former Senate candidate in Virginia and retired navy captain, has been the acting secretary since April and was previously the under secretary. “The Senate needs to confirm this Warfighter, ASAP, so he can continue the fantastic work he has been doing over the past 4 months,” Trump said of the nomination. The news comes amid a shake up in US military leadership under defense secretary Pete Hegseth. This week army secretary Daniel Driscoll left his role after 18 months on the job, prompting Democrats to accuse Hegseth of having “hollowed out” the army’s senior ranks. The US House of Representative has voted to censure Chuck Edwards, a Republican congressman who the ethics committee found violated rules against sexual harassment in his conduct towards two young female staffers. The vote was 413-2, with 207 Republicans joining 205 Democrats. The largely ceremonial punishment saw Edwards stand in the well of the House chamber and be read the resolution. First elected in 2022 to represent a western North Carolina district, Edwards dropped his bid for re-election following the release of the bipartisan panel’s determination that he “may have created or fostered a hostile work environment and engaged in sexual harassment” by giving gifts and lavishing attention on the two women. “A member of Congress should not single out a staffer and isolate them from other staff, make frequent comments regarding that person’s appearance and weight, send messages in the middle of the night, text staff deeply personal and seemingly romantic thoughts, intrude on personal occasions without invitation, pay for personal vacations, and spend thousands of dollars on gifts for staffers,” the report read. In a speech on the House floor before the vote, Edwards defended himself, noting that the committee found he did not engage in sexual activity with the staffers or suggested it. He argued the ethics committee overreached in its conclusions, while apologizing both to the unnamed staffers and his wife. “Regret is not an admission of sexual harassment, I can acknowledge poor judgment, regret the discomfort that some of my actions may have caused, and apologize to those who were hurt by this episode, while still disputing a conclusion that the evidence just simply does not support,” Edwards said. North Carolina Republicans have replaced him on the ballot with state representative Jennifer Balkcom, who will face the Democratic nominee Jamie Ager in the November midterms. Kathy Hochul, New York’s governor, criticized Donald Trump for withholding $87m in counterterrorism funds from the state, describing the move as a betrayal of 9/11 victims. “Don’t undermine our public safety efforts. Don’t defund the police who thwart terror attacks. Don’t play political games with people’s lives,” Hochul said at a press conference
chineseTitle: “危险的权力攫取”：民主党高层谴责可能阻碍邮寄投票的美国邮政系统 - 现场直播
chineseSummary: 一位民主党参议员披露了一份举报声明，该声明警告称，美国邮政总局将推出一个可能破坏邮寄投票的计算机系统，可能会出现混乱。
chineseContent: 哈基姆·杰弗里斯谴责特朗普政府对海地大学生皮埃尔·达马斯·贝尔之死的回应，皮埃尔·达马斯·贝尔在失去合法身份并被要求佩戴脚踝监视器后自杀身亡。这位众议院民主党领袖表示，“像数十万海地人一样，皮埃尔逃离了危险的环境，获得了临时保护身份，为自己建设更好的生活，并为我们的国家做出爱国贡献”，并将政府的行为描述为“令人鄙视的残忍行为”。 “相反，唐纳德·特朗普的大规模驱逐机器剥夺了皮埃尔的合法地位，用可怕的暴力威胁他，强迫他戴上脚踝监视器，并在同龄人面前羞辱他。”贝尔是一名 20 岁的男子，于 2024 年来到美国，并于 7 月失去了临时保护身份，于周一去世。 NBC 新闻报道称，虽然贝尔的移民案已在法庭上审理，但 ICE 要求他佩戴脚踝监视器。贝尔说，他对这次经历感到“羞辱”并受到欺凌。周二，参议员埃德·马基(Ed Markey)在马萨诸塞州赢得了民主党初选，击败了国会议员塞斯·莫尔顿(Seth Moulton)的挑战，塞斯·莫尔顿试图通过向选民争论他的对手太老了，无法有效地完成工作来推翻他。马萨诸塞州的民主党人占主导地位，这使得这位参议员有望在 11 月大选中赢得第三个完整任期，届时他将面临共和党提名人约翰·迪顿 (John Deaton)。据美联社报道，这位 80 岁的现任总统轻松击败了 47 岁的对手，此时民主党选民正为一些议员的年龄而苦恼，而乔·拜登在 2024 年的灾难性连任竞选以及卡马拉·哈里斯随后未能阻止唐纳德·特朗普重返白宫，加剧了这种担忧。特朗普政府没收了
